Debrief DB-021
1) The actor ran a spoofed GNSS base-station emulator broadcasting corrected ephemeris and timing, causing the drones' dead-reckoning loops to drift; this produced the logged "GNSS fix loss" entries and the 40-meter route deviation traces saved in the fleet telemetry dump.
2) The actor deployed a directional 5.9 GHz transceiver emitting ADS-B/Mode-S style position reports from a rooftop, tricking the delivery network's traffic manager into re-routing; the artifact was the anomalous Mode-S hex blocks captured in the airport's ADS-B feed and the corresponding re-tasking messages in the dispatch log.
3) The actor flashed a modified firmware image onto a captured ground station using a JTAG probe to silently inject a "return-to-home" beacon override; the concrete artifact was the extracted binary diff showing the injected beacon table and the matching CRC hash in the staging repository.
4) The actor used a laptop with a software-defined radio to replay a captured Wi-Fi management frame (deauth storm) against the drones' mesh links, simulating a routine access-point outage; the artifact was the 802.11 capture file with the forged deauthentication frames and the matching "AP unreachable" entries in the drone logs.
5) The actor spoofed a TLS-terminated command channel by standing up a rogue certificate with a look-alike CN and MITMing the telemetry uplink, which made the operator console display a benign "transient network error" banner; the artifact was the forged certificate chain and the console screenshot saved to evidence folder 021-B.
6) The actor placed a low-power RF jammer tuned to the drones' 2.4 GHz control band and cycled it on a pseudo-random schedule to mimic environmental interference; the produced artifact was the spectrum-analyzer trace showing the pulsed noise floor and the drones' "signal degradation" fault codes in the maintenance ticket.
7) The actor planted a fake GPS antenna feed on the ground station's calibration port to bias the position estimate toward the drop site; the artifact was the annotated oscilloscope capture of the injected 1 PPS offset and the ground station's internal calibration log showing the 220-meter bias.
8) The actor scheduled the interference to fire only during the fleet's known mid-route waypoint transitions, reducing the chance of a manual operator noticing; the artifact was the cron entry in the attacker's laptop shell history and the timestamped flight-plan overlap chart.
9) The actor exfiltrated the collected package manifests through a steganographic channel inside benign-looking weather telemetry packets, so the data flow blended with normal operations; the artifact was the decoded image frames recovered from the outbound UDP stream, each embedding a fragment of the manifest CSV.
10) The actor pre-positioned a "spare" landing pad with a matching RFID tag at the intercept site so the drones' landing-confirmation routine accepted it as a legitimate drop zone; the artifact was the RFID tag dump and the landing-success ACK logged by the affected drones within 90 seconds of each other.
